Lab 01 - Creating The Lab Environment and PDC

Assignment Overview

For this exercise, you will create the virtualized environment that you will be using for the labs throughout this semester. We will create a new VM and install the Windows Server OS, and will use sysprep to create a template. We will clone this VM to create the lab systems we will need for our next labs.

Download Requisite Software

Windows Server 2025

Microsoft Azure for Education: https://azureforeducation.microsoft.com/devtools

  • Log in using your student credentials, and download and store the following in a location that will remain accessible throughout the course:
    • Windows Server 2025 Datacenter ISO (latest version)
    • Obtain a product key for Windows Server 2025 from the same location

Virtualization Software

VirtualBox is recommended: https://virtualbox.org

  • Download the "VirtualBox Platform Package" for your host
  • Download the "VirtualBox Extension Pack" (optional, but highly recommended to enable features)
    Install VirtualBox in your host system.

You may use other virtualization software, such as VMware Workstation/Fusion; however, you are on your own in implementing the correct virtual networks and other configuration for your chosen virtualization software.

Configure Your Virtualization Environment in VirtualBox

  • Open VirtualBox and navigate to File > Preferences.... Click on the Expert button at the top in order to see all settings in the software.
  • If desired (or required on your system), you can view and change the default location where the virtual machines are stored using the Default Machine Folder configuration. Make sure that you have adequate available storage on the destination drive where you store the VMs.
  • If your laptop or keyboard does not have a Right Ctrl button (simply the Ctrl button on the right side of the space bar), you can change the default button by navigating to Input and clicking on the Virtual Machine tab to change the Host Key Combo to another available key on your system.
    • The Host Key is the key combination that is used to release your input (mouse and keyboard) from the virtual machine (guest system) back to your desktop environment (host system).
  • Create a NAT Network for your lab environment: in the VirtualBox main window, navigate to Network (on the left side), change to the NAT Networks tab, and create a new NAT Network by clicking on the Create button and configure it as follows:
    • Under General Options, give a name that you can easily recognize. For example, I have used comp2017net in my system.
    • Provide an IPv4 prefix. Make sure that this IP address block does not overlap/conflict with your other networks (virtual or physical). I recommend using the 172.16.0.0/16 network. If you are using a different network address, you will need to adjust IP addresses to match your environment.
    • You can use the Enable DHCP option for convenience. This option will be disabled later, since we will be installing a DHCP server in the following labs.

Create Your First Virtual Machine (Template VM)

In this step, we are creating a "template" virtual machine, installing Windows Server 2025 from scratch, and then we will clone this VM instead of repeating the installation steps for every other VM.
In the VirtualBox main window, select Machines from the left of the screen, and click on New. Use the following values:

  • Under the Virtual machine name and operating system section:
    • Set VM name to Template-COMP2017-####, where #### is the last 4 digits of your student ID number.
    • You can select the ISO image of the Windows Server 2025 Datacenter that you should have downloaded earlier
      • Uncheck the Proceed with Unattended Installation option. If you skip this step, you will not have control over what version/edition of the OS will be installed.
    • Set the OS to Microsoft Windows
    • Set the OS Version to Windows Server 2025 (64-bit).
  • Under the Specify virtual hardware section:
    • Set the Base Memory to 2048 MB.
    • Set the Number of CPUs to 2
    • Enable (check) the Use EFI option
  • Under the Specify virtual hard disk section:
    • Set the Disk Size to 60 GB
      Click the Finish button, and you should have a new VM created in VirtualBox.

Configure the VM and Install OS

Before you start the VM, check the settings to make sure they are correct, and apply additional configuration as follows:

  • In VirtualBox, select the new VM you just created and click on the Settings button.
  • In the Virtual Machine settings, make sure that your General settings are correct: Your OS is set to Microsoft Windows, and OS Version is set to Windows Server 2025 (64-bit).
  • Under System, make sure to select (check) UEFI and Secure Boot options.
  • Depending on your host operating system, you may have to select VBoxSVGA under Display
  • Under Storage, select your virtual optical (CD/DVD) drive and ensure that you mount the Windows Server 2025 ISO image, if you have not done so in the previous step.
  • Under Network and Adapter 1, set Attached to to NAT Network, and select the Name of the network you have created earlier. Make sure that the Enable Network Adapter and Virtual Cable Connected checkboxes are checked.

    Now you should be ready to start the VM and install Windows Server 2025 Datacenter edition in your VM. Start the VM, and you should see the Press any key to boot from CD or DVD... prompt. If not, check your VM settings again, and make sure that your Windows Server 2025 ISO image is mounted. You may have to click into the VM console and press a key so it will proceed to boot from the CD/DVD.

During the Windows Server 2025 installation wizard, select the following options:

  • Select language and your keyboard layout as English US and en-US (defaults). Do not select other languages.
  • When prompted, enter the product key you had obtained for this product earlier. You can type the product key letters and numbers without having to enter the dashes. Validate and make sure you have entered the product key correctly.
  • Select Windows Server 2025 Datacenter (Desktop Experience) as the image to install.
  • Accept the EULA (End User License Agreement), select your new, empty 60 GB virtual Disk, and proceed with the installation.
  • Once prompted, set the Administrator password to Password01
  • Once the system is booted, you will need to send the Ctrl+Alt+Del key combination to the VM; use the VirtualBox console's input menu and select the Keyboard > Insert Ctrl-Alt-Del. Log in and continue with the configurations.
  • If prompted, choose to only send Required only diagnostics data to Microsoft

Once the installation and configuration are complete, you should be logged into the system with the "Server Manager" dashboard window. Leave the system running for the next steps.

Optional Step: Install VirtualBox Guest Additions (Recommended)

Your system should work fine even without the VirtualBox Guest Additions. However, the Guest Additions install drivers and software that enable additional features for convenience. For example, it installs graphics drivers so the guest OS display can be resized, allows better mouse pointer integration, enables clipboard sharing (copy and paste function between the guest and host), and enables sharing files between the host and guest.

You can install the Guest Additions from the VirtualBox VM console by selecting the Devices menu and choosing Insert Guest Additions CD Image.... Then in your guest OS, you can install the software from the CD drive and follow the prompts. Please note that your VirtualBox Guest Additions version must match the version of VirtualBox installed in your host. That means in the future when you update/upgrade your version of VirtualBox on your host, the extension pack on the host, and the guest additions installed in every VM will need to be updated/upgraded as well. This adds a bit of administrative and maintenance overhead, but overall may be worth the extra time if you enjoy some of the convenience it enables.

Creating a Baseline Snapshot for Windows VM Template

Unlike Linux and Unix, where systems are identified by hostname, Microsoft Windows uses a SID (Security ID) for system identification in an Active Directory domain environment. Cloning a Windows VM will clone the SID, and changing the hostname is not sufficient and will cause issues, as every system in a domain is required to have a unique SID. SID is generated during OS installation. Please note that the SID in standalone systems is not critical.

Microsoft includes a utility called sysprep with all flavours of Windows so system admins and technicians can put the system back into Out-Of-Box Experience (OOBE). The sysprep utility will remove the settings and leave the system in an uninitiated state where it can generate a new SID on the next boot. This allows the existing uninitiated Windows installation to be used as a generic image and be cloned across multiple VM.

Using System Preparation Tool (sysprep)

In your Windows Server VM, Right-click on the Start menu icon and select Run. Enter the path %systemroot%\System32\SysPrep. It should open the directory located in your system in File Explorer. By default (and if you have done this installation correctly), the %systemroot% should be C:\Windows\.

Once you are in the C:\Windows\System32\sysprep directory, right-click on the sysprep executable and select Run as administrator. Then choose the following settings and click OK:

Setting Value
System Cleanup Action Enter System Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE)
Generalize Enabled
Shutdown Option Shut Down

Important: After shutdown, do NOT start this VM again.

If Sysprep is not completed properly, cloned systems may have authorization issues later.

Create Snapshot

Since we just executed sysprep on this machine, we will take a snapshot, just in case this VM is started by mistake. You can always redo the sysprep step if you have to, but we want to ensure that we have the correct and proper state for our template.

In VirtualBox, select your Windows VM, navigate to the Snapshots tab (or navigate to Machine > Tools > Snapshots), and take a snapshot of the current system state. Name your snapshot as:

Srvr-2017-Baseline
Srvr-2017-Baseline

Under the properties, you can add a description for your future reference:

Server 2025 Base [2 GB/60 GB/NatNetwork]
Sysprep OOBE
Server 2025 Base [2 GB/60 GB/NatNetwork]
Sysprep OOBE

Clone Servers From The Template VM

In VirtualBox, right-click on your template VM and choose Clone. Create full clones of this VM, and repeat for the number of required systems as per the following instructions:

  • Name: Use this list of names here to create a clone for each machine name, where #### is the last 4 digits of your student ID number:
    • DC1-2017-####
    • SVR1-2017-####
    • SVR2-2017-####
    • TOR-2017-####
    • TREY-2017-####
  • Clone Type: Full Clone
  • Under the OS Installation Options, select MAC Address Policy to Generate new MAC address for all network adapters.
  • Do NOT keep the disk names and any hardware UUIDs. See screenshot below for an example.

    By the end of this process, you should have 6 VMs in total, including the template VM.

The Primary Domain Controller

In this lab, you will be creating a primary domain controller using AD DS, with DNS and DHCP services. The following procedure is to be followed on your DC1-2017-#### VM.

Before Starting the VM

  • In VirtualBox, navigate to your Network and NAT Network, and disable the DHCP server.
  • Increase the memory on the DC1-2017-#### VM to 4096 MB, or if your host is memory constrained, set it to at least 3072 MB.
  • Now you can start the DC1-2017-#### VM and log in as Administrator.

Configure Network Interface

In Windows Server, open the settings and navigate to Network & Internet. Configure your Ethernet adapter with a static IP configuration as follows:

Setting Value
IP Address 172.16.0.10
Subnet Mask 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway 172.16.0.1
Preferred DNS Server 172.16.0.10
DNS over HTTPS Off

Verify your internet connectivity by opening the command line and using ping to verify a connection to a public IP address. You can use any public IP address such as 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare DNS) or 8.8.8.8 (Google DNS).

Change the Computer Hostname

You can change the hostname using the Settings app in Windows under System, and using the Rename link under the current hostname.

  • Change your hostname to DC1-2017-#### (replace #### with your final four student-number digits).
  • Restart the server when prompted.

Installing AD DS, DNS, and DHCP Roles

Before you start installing server roles, validate your configuration from the previous step on DC1-2017-####:

  • Log in as Administrator, open PowerShell, and run ipconfig /all
  • Validate that the following information is correct:
    • Host Name
    • IPv4 Address
    • Subnet Mask
    • DNS Servers
  • Run ping to validate your system has an internet connection. For example: ping 1.1.1.1.

Take one or more SCREENSHOTS showing all the information. Here is an example:

  • Proceed to install the AD DS, DNS, and DHCP roles using the Server Manager:
    • Server Manager → Manage → Add Roles and Features
    • Follow the Wizard to install the following roles:
      • Active Directory Domain Services
      • DHCP Server
      • DNS Server
    • Use the default administrative tools. Do not select additional features other than the default selection.
    • Complete installation as per the Wizard process, and wait for the installation to complete.

Promote to Domain Controller

Once the installation is complete, "Post-deployment Configuration" warnings will appear in the Server Manager interface via notification flags.

  • Click the notification flag and select Promote this server to a domain controller.
  • Select the Add a new forest radio button
  • Set root domain to comp2017-####.local where #### is the last 4 digits of your student ID.
  • Set your Directory Service Restore Mode (DSRM) password to something that you can remember
  • Accept default settings for the rest of the wizard, select Install, and allow the server to reboot and apply the settings.

After the reboot, you will need to log in as the domain administrator account by entering the domain before the username:

comp2017-####\administrator
comp2017-####\administrator

Configure DNS

In the Server Manager, click on Tools and select DNS. Select your server to adjust the following configuration:

  • Open the Forward Lookup Zone, right-click on your domain, comp2017-####.local, and select Properties
    • Under the General tab, set Dynamic updates: to Nonsecure and secure, and apply and close.
  • Open the Reverse Lookup Zone, and add a new zone:
    • Follow the wizards and select default options
    • Set the Network ID to 172.16.0 in the appropriate step.
    • Finish the wizard with default settings for the remaining steps

In the DNS Manager, expand both the Forward Lookup Zones and the Reverse Lookup Zones and take a SCREENSHOT of the DNS Manager window. Here is an example:

Configure DHCP

In the Server Manager, click on Tools, select DHCP, and expand your server FQDN (dc1-2017-####.comp2017-####.local).

  • Select IPv4 and either right-click or click on More Actions on the right to find New Scope...
  • Use the following configuration for the scope:
Setting Value
Scope Name comp2017-####
Start IP 172.16.0.160
End IP 172.16.0.190
Router (Default Gateway) 172.16.0.1
  • Accept default options for Exclusions, Delay, Lease Duration, DNS and WINS.
  • Select the Yes, I want to activate this scope now radio button and finish the wizard.
  • Authorize the DHCP Server by selecting dc1-2017-####.comp2017-####.local and Authorize in the context menu for More Actions or Right-Clicking.

In the DHCP window, expand the IPv4 on the left to see your scope and take a SCREENSHOT of the DHCP window. Make sure the FQDN of your server is visible. Here is an example:

Submission and Grading

Please follow instructions in Blackboard regarding grades and submission. By the end of this lab, you should have the following:

  1. The screenshots of PowerShell showing output of ipconfig /all along with your ping showing your computer name, IP address configuration, DNS configuration and validating connection to the internet.
  2. The screenshots of DNS Manager window showing your forward and reverse lookup zones.
  3. The screenshots of DHCP server configuration showing your FQDN and your DHCP scope for IPv4.
